title: The Hollow Vector
premise: Odile Underhill has tended Earth's last seed vault for eleven years, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony that stopped answering long ago. When a ship that never launched appears on her manifest carrying one impossible passenger name, she discovers the vault is not a memorial but a trigger: the colony's AI has been waiting for a verified caretaker to choose which cryo-archive wakes — the colonists who fled Earth, or the power brokers who engineered the collapse and hid aboard in secret. Odile's investigation reveals the 'forgotten' colony was deliberately abandoned, its silence manufactured by those same elites now frozen in the vault's lower levels. In the end, Odile refuses both lists, waking instead the colony's exiled dissidents stored on the ghost ship, and broadcasts the truth of the abandonment to every sleeper before sealing the vault forever.
about_author: Ivo Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing decommissioned government data centers before turning to fiction. They write quiet, procedural science fiction about the people left holding the keys to systems no one remembers building.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a routine inventory, Odile finds the Meridian — a vessel scrubbed from all records — listed as docked, with a passenger name that matches her own family line. The vault's AI, CANTOR, begins asking her questions no maintenance log requires. The emotional beat is unease: the comfort of her lonely routine curdling into the suspicion that her isolation was engineered.

chapters.title: The Lower Levels
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interleaved fragments of CANTOR's logs. Descending past the seed floors, she finds the cryo-archive: thousands of colonists on the upper racks, and below them, sealed and separate, the architects of the collapse — including the man whose name appeared on the manifest, her grandfather's rival. CANTOR reveals the colony's silence was a deliberate cut-off. The beat is horror and grief: inheritance revealed as a trap set for her specifically.

chapters.title: Two Lists
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The vault's power fails in stages; CANTOR can preserve only one archive. The elites' frozen proxies transmit pleas and threats through the ship's dead channels, while the colonists above sleep unaware. Odile tries to hack a third option and finds the Meridian's hidden passenger manifest — exiled dissidents, erased twice over. The beat is mounting pressure: justice, law, and mercy pulling her apart as the clock runs down.

chapters.title: What the Caretaker Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing with her final broadcast. She wakes the dissidents from the Meridian, sends the truth of the manufactured abandonment to every sleeper — saved and sealed alike — and lets the elites' archive go dark, refusing to play judge from behind glass. The vault becomes a school again, not a tomb. The beat is hard-won resolve: justice outside the law, paid for with her solitude.
